source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Regarding AXP2101, is there a simpler way to handle the power system? The battery must be chargeable while the device is operating, and both 3.3V and 5V rails are required. If a better and simpler implementation exists, please suggest it.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Above all, the design must use the battery efficiently so the device can operate for as long as possible.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Although AXP provides exactly the functionality I need and includes advanced features, it also requires many static external components, so I am unsure whether to retain it. I know about TP4056 and similar alternatives, but I do not think they handle charging and powering the system simultaneously very well.

ambiguity.description: The client has not yet decided whether to retain AXP2101 or replace it with a simpler power-management implementation that still supports simultaneous charging and operation.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Good, then let's keep the current power-management component.

routing_warnings.description: The statement specifically establishes operation without a battery, for which the inventory contains a narrower Requirement.
The AXP specification check concerns the narrower no-battery operating behavior and is not runtime verification of the overall power-management architecture.
The observed L3 voltage instability and partial manufacturing yield directly concern DCDC1 regulation.
The concrete failure reported here is native USB enumeration; the brief successful rail startup does not verify the complete power-management Requirement.
The suspected USBLC6 VBUS wiring error concerns the narrower USB ESD-protection Requirement.
The rail-collapse, low regulation, transient instability, and DCDC1 deterioration form a distinct execution trajectory for the narrower DCDC1 regulation Requirement.
The unsuccessful AXP2101 replacement is follow-up evidence in the persistent DCDC1 failure investigation, not a change to the selected power-management architecture.
